title: Comprehensive reanalysis of second archive batch
methodology: Computed SHA-256 from each uploaded byte stream.
Decompressed -lh0- and -lh5- payloads with repository parsers.
Scanned extracted text for API symbols, message commands, structures, includes, and lifecycle evidence.
Compared every upload with canonical archive bytes.
Did not infer semantics solely from filenames or undecoded payloads.

reviewed_finding.finding: SDK contains C, assembler, Amiga E and documentation for a broad message-command interface; numeric command tables are documented but kept separate from MAXs semantics.
Contains library, FD file, C bindings and documentation; confirms a callable Amiga shared-library interface rather than a message-port protocol.
Documentation-only package; useful for ecosystem context but no source-level API implementation was found.
Documentation confirms Paragon compatibility and the practical command boundary above command 21.
Bridge payload and text establish interoperability context, but no readable source-level API definitions were present.
MAXDoor.e defines DoorControl/DoorReply messaging and wrappers for commands 1, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 20 and 200.
Documentation describes recovery/maintenance use around MAXs/Paragon doors; no source API corpus is included.
ARexx and documentation demonstrate FAME menu/text integration, but not a general native DoorPort implementation.
Amiga E launcher and documentation confirm Function 34 execution context and runtime packaging behavior.
Large FAMECommands guide documents FAMEDoorMsg/FAMEDoorPort and a broad command surface, including structured conference, mail and user operations.
Earlier FCOMM distribution corroborates the same DoorPort message model and provides historical version comparison material.
DoorHeader documentation provides integration constants and startup context for FAME doors.
E modules expose external user, transfer, file, board and menu structures, confirming a typed binding layer.
Assembler includes expose BBSBase/BBSMenu and detailed user-record offsets, independently corroborating the AmBoS data model.
Developer guide, C headers and FD file define BBS.library structures and entry points; this is the strongest AmBoS primary source in the batch.
